question: A 25-year-old woman comes to the physician because of pain and weakness in her right forearm and hand for several months. Two years ago, she sustained a fracture of her ulnar shaft with dislocation of the radial head that was treated surgically. Physical examination shows mild tenderness a few centimeters distal to the lateral epicondyle. She has marked weakness when attempting to extend her right middle finger. There is radial deviation on extension of the wrist. Sensation is not impaired. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fracture of ulnar shaft with dislocation of radial head" -> "Surgical treatment" -> "Possible nerve entrapment or damage during or post-surgery" -> "Weakness in extending middle finger and radial deviation of wrist" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve involvement" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Pain and weakness in right forearm and hand" -> "History of ulnar shaft fracture and radial head dislocation" -> "Physical examination shows tenderness near lateral epicondyle and specific motor deficits" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve controls middle finger extension and wrist extension without sensory loss" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve is most likely affected" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Marked weakness in extending right middle finger" -> "Radial deviation on wrist extension" -> "No sensory impairment" -> "Symptoms localized to motor function controlled by posterior interosseous nerve" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve dysfunction" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Previous surgical intervention on forearm" -> "Development of symptoms months after surgery" -> "Localized tenderness and specific motor weakness without sensory deficits" -> "Involvement of a nerve that does not affect sensation but controls finger and wrist extension" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve likely affected" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Fracture and dislocation treated surgically" -> "Chronic pain and weakness in specific forearm regions" -> "Physical signs of motor impairment in actions like finger extension" -> "Lack of sensory loss points away from nerves like ulnar or superficial radial" -> "Posterior interosseous nerve likely implicated due to its motor function role" -> 95%
analysis: The patient's symptoms include weakness in extending the middle finger and radial deviation upon wrist extension, without sensory loss. These symptoms suggest an issue with a nerve that primarily controls motor function to the extensor muscles of the forearm. The posterior interosseous nerve, a branch of the radial nerve, fits this description as it innervates the extensor muscles of the forearm and does not carry significant sensory fibers. The ulnar nerve primarily affects the medial hand and fingers, the anterior interosseous nerve affects flexor muscles, the superficial radial nerve is primarily sensory, and the musculocutaneous nerve affects the anterior compartment of the arm. Therefore, the posterior interosseous nerve is the most likely affected nerve in this scenario.
